question: Can P1 protect current scalar predictions from residual h_vec state freedom by classifying higher-shell residuals as perturbations rather than background normalization freedoms?

executive_verdict.summary: Yes. P1 does not select the full h_vec state, but it separates exact-background data from perturbative carrier data. Residual higher-shell freedom cannot be used as a hidden background normalization parameter for current scalar observables.

definitions.name: Exact P1 Background Sector
definitions.definition: Schwarzschild horizon radius and mass parameter, closed K=+1 OS support geometry, round horizon symmetry, banked Hawking-compatible active quotient, and framework constants fixed independently of residual h_vec shell-tail choices.

definitions.name: h_vec Perturbation Sector
definitions.definition: Gauge/null-reduced coexact one-particle carrier used by the Paper 23 scalar bridge and upgraded by the Paper 27 Spatial CCR Lift Theorem.

definitions.name: Background-Normalization Freedom
definitions.definition: A variable changeable while leaving the exact P1 background interpretation intact and changing a current cosmological prediction.

definitions.name: Higher-Shell Residual Diagnostic
definitions.definition: Observable or diagnostic functional on h_vec that reads covariance outside the rank-one scalar-amplitude quotient, such as O_n(G)=Tr(P_n G P_n).

theorems.name: Higher-Shell Residuals Are Not Exact-Background Normalizations
theorems.claim: A nonzero higher-shell residual diagnostic on h_vec is not a background normalization freedom of the exact P1 sector.

theorems.name: Higher-Shell Diagnostics Are Future Perturbative Observables If Physical
theorems.claim: If a higher-shell residual diagnostic is physical and not gauge/null or backreaction-forbidden, it is a perturbative observable of the h_vec sector, not a hidden parameter in the current scalar-amplitude chain.

theorems.name: P1 Background/Perturbation Separation for h_vec
theorems.claim: Residual higher-shell freedom on h_vec cannot be used as a hidden background normalization parameter for current IO scalar observables. It is scalar-quotient null, a perturbative observable, a backreaction-constrained deformation, gauge/null, or a separately fixed exterior import.

theorems.name: Full State Selection Remains Open but Non-Damaging for Current Scalar Predictions
theorems.claim: The full ambient h_vec state remains open, but that open status does not create a hidden fitted parameter in current scalar predictions.

recommended_wording: The full state on h_vec is not selected in this paper. This is not a hidden normalization freedom for the scalar amplitude. P1 separates exact-background data from perturbative carrier data: residual higher-shell covariance either is null under the scalar bridge quotient, is constrained by backreaction, is gauge/null, is separately fixed by imported exterior physics, or becomes a future perturbative observable. It is not adjustable inside the current scalar prediction chain.
must_not_overclaim: Do not claim P1 selects the full h_vec state.
Do not claim higher-shell h_vec observables are unphysical.
Do not claim full state selection is no longer open.
Do not treat future perturbative observables as hidden background parameters.
